Use case: logo-brand.
Transform the typography idea in the supplied reference into a new, professionally art-directed static lettering study for Lotus Flow. Input image: STYLE REFERENCE ONLY. Focus exclusively on the AVANT GARDE masthead at the top of the magazine; ignore browser UI, magazine illustration and surrounding screenshot.

Create ONE clean typographic artboard on warm off-white paper. The main exact text is "EXPRESSION OVER IMPRESSION". All three words must be spelled correctly, each once. Design a compact, sculptural masthead with two dominant tightly fitted lines EXPRESSION and IMPRESSION; OVER is a smaller red linking word placed in a carefully designed negative space between them. The main lettering is deep black.

Crucial: closely follow the bespoke 1970s geometric Avant Garde masthead structure in the reference. True circular O and curved P/R bowls, highly geometric triangular diagonals, one consistent elegant medium-bold stroke weight (do not make it a grotesk extra-bold block font). Draw intentional, clever bespoke ligatures: E-X joined through a cut diagonal, P-R sharing a stem and bowl junction, R-E connecting through the R diagonal, I-O-N as an interlocked geometric unit. Use the reference's diagonal shared strokes and extremely close counters. The outlines must look like a skilled lettering designer redrew the actual words, not typeset a normal sans-serif then squeezed or tracked it. Maintain legibility and clean expertly adjusted counters. Avoid generic Montserrat/Futura look, uniform rows of loose standalone letters, overlapping letters without a real shared-stroke redesign, swashes, bubbly letters, 3D effects or artificial graphic decoration.

The entire composition should feel like an original iconic avant-garde music magazine masthead, confidently Pop and refined. Very subtle paper grain, crisp edges, generous outer margin. Below in small restrained typography put only "LOTUS FLOW — DISPLAY LETTERING". No other text, no browser mockup, no poster art, no branding borrowed from the reference.
chinese:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Transform the supplied Chinese "玻璃心" lettering reference into an ORIGINAL hand-designed static Chinese title artwork. Input image is a style reference for translucent glass stroke planes and spatial depth. Do not reproduce the original page, labels or blue/pink color scheme.

Exact main title, with all five characters readable and correctly written: "精选作品集". No other text. Wide artboard, warm near-black charcoal background, restrained soft studio lighting, title occupies the central 75% with breathing room.

The user wants expressive, irregular, free-spirited, soulful lettering, NOT a strict regular modular font. A brilliant Chinese lettering artist has redrawn the five characters from scratch as a single lively composition: different character sizes, unequal spacing, subtly rising/falling rhythm, different stroke lengths and weights, unexpected but legible asymmetries. Mix folded angular strokes with a few soft curving, curling or tapering strokes and generous irregular counters. Some radicals can gently reach toward their neighbors; the overall flow feels musical and alive, balanced by human judgment. Preserve recognizable Chinese character anatomy; do not turn it into random abstract sculpture. Avoid mechanical grids, uniform chopped planks, identical thickness, aligned repeated frames, repeating parallelograms, standard typefaces with a 3D extrusion.

Materials: the dominant FRONT/body of the strokes is luminous white translucent optical glass, with precise glossy edges, beautiful internal refraction and subtly frosted broad faces so the white lettering stays readable. Depth, side surfaces and projected shadows are ruby red and deep crimson. A mostly white glass title with red undersides/shadows, not solid red letters with white outlines. Each stroke has individually designed spatial thickness and orientation, some gently twisted, a few irregular carved facets. The material should feel physically convincing yet poetic, delicate and premium. Not chrome, not pearl plastic, not chunky origami blocks. Restrained highlights and red shadow, no overpowering neon glow, no rainbow or extra colors.

The result must look like a finished high-end experimental Chinese display lettering artwork, hand designed and evocative, with beautifully irregular rhythm. Give the five characters a natural connected spirit rather than five equally sized separate squares.
